moat_against: ROIC proxy below cost of capital for a decade (0.5-6.4%, 5.11% in 2025) — pricing power has not produced excess returns
Fiserv and Jack Henry competition; Jack Henry holds community-bank niche with ~98% retention FIS has not penetrated
Bank consolidation shrinks the client base; cloud-native cores are lowering switching barriers
Serial large M&A (Worldpay bought 2019, largely written down and exited 2024-26) destroyed capital and left high leverage
moat_for: Mission-critical core banking and issuer processing with high switching costs and multi-year recurring contracts
Scale after Issuer Solutions (TSYS) acquisition: world's largest issuer processor, 40B+ transactions/yr, clients in 75+ countries
Recurring-revenue base: pro forma recurring revenue growth 4.8% in Q1 2026, gross margin improved 33.2% (2016) to 36.9% (2025)
Integrated banking + issuing stack for large and super-regional banks that smaller rivals cannot match
moat_justification: Real switching costs in mission-critical core banking and issuer processing (multi-year contracts, now the largest global issuer processor after the Jan 2026 Issuer Solutions deal, 40B+ transactions/yr), but a decade of ROIC proxy at 0.5-6.4% (fundamentals.json: 1.25% in 2021, 1.98% in 2022, 2.93% in 2023, 4.71% in 2024, 5.11% in 2025) — below the cost of capital through the cycle — proves the franchise has not converted that stickiness into excess returns; gross margin only 33.2% (2016) to 36.9% (2025). Moderate/narrow moat, not wide.
name: Fidelity National Information Services, Inc.
one_liner: Sticky but low-return processor, moat 5/10 — clears 15% on the TTM base (18.6% weighted, IV $46.72 vs $35.94) but the band runs C to A, leverage stepped up again for Issuer Solutions, and 2026 pro forma guidance was already cut; size it like the bear end (C, 14.6%), not the weighted B.
sector: Financial technology / banking and issuer processing
